sources.note: Trains separate Top-K sparse autoencoders on a reasoning model's activations in thinking and non-thinking modes, and finds that suppressing the most active reasoning features destroys mathematical formatting as reliably as it destroys reasoning -- with the model responding by generating 454 percent more tokens of lower-diversity, more metacognitively marked text rather than stopping.
sources.title: Thinking vs. NoThinking: Towards Interpreting Reasoning Mechanisms of Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders

sources.note: Shows on four internal Netflix verification tasks that explicit reasoning usually degrades subjective judgement, that applying RLVR to fix it makes the policy abandon deliberation for short heuristic guessing, and that a length bonus gated on answer correctness is what stops the collapse.
sources.title: LLM Reasoning for Subjective Tasks: Failure Modes, Mitigation, and Dynamic Reasoning Routing

sources.note: Separates reasoning into procedural advancement and 'epistemic verbalization' — the token-level externalization of uncertainty — and shows that emitting doubt is what lets a model recover from silent divergence, that injecting a bare doubt cue recovers failed trajectories, and that 800 SFT examples suffice to install or destroy the habit.
sources.title: Understanding Reasoning in LLMs through Strategic Information Allocation under Uncertainty

result.definition: A model abandoning deliberation for a short heuristic answer under training pressure, and across 3 sources a failure distinct from entropy collapse because it is about length and structure rather than about distributional narrowing. Its clearest measurement: on subjective judgement tasks the mean terminated completion length falls from about 300 tokens to about 170 after roughly 70 steps of verifiable-reward training, because guessing the label earns the same or higher reward at a fraction of the token cost -- the inverse of the length-and-accuracy-rise signature of successful mathematical training. A second form is the opposite: suppressing a model's most active reasoning features makes it generate 454 percent more tokens of lower-diversity, more metacognitively marked text rather than stopping. And a third is behavioural: suppressing the habit of verbalising uncertainty halves competition accuracy across five models despite every training trace being correct.
